questions.q: State two activities carried out in the analysis stage of the program development life cycle.
ms: identifying the problem / requirements (what the program must do)
abstraction – removing unnecessary detail
decomposition – breaking the problem into smaller parts
identifying inputs, processes, outputs and storage
questions.model: In the analysis stage the programmer identifies the requirements of the problem and uses abstraction to remove unnecessary details.

questions.q:
Describe the shape and use of each of these flowchart symbols:
(a) terminator [1]
(b) process [1]
(c) subroutine (predefined process). [1]
ms: (a) rounded rectangle / oval – marks the start or end (START / STOP) of the algorithm
(b) rectangle – an action / calculation / assignment, e.g. Total ← Total + Mark
(c) rectangle with double vertical lines at each side – calls a subroutine / predefined procedure
questions.model:
(a) A terminator is a rounded rectangle used for START and STOP.
(b) A process is a rectangle used for an action or calculation, such as Total ← Total + Mark.
(c) A subroutine is a rectangle with a double line at each side, used to call a predefined procedure or function.

questions.q: A cinema wants a program to sell tickets. Explain what is meant by a structure diagram and give an example of one for this system, showing at least two levels below the top. (Write the diagram as an indented list.)
ms: a structure diagram shows the decomposition of a system into sub-systems / smaller tasks (1)
hierarchical / top-down – each level breaks the level above into more detail (1)
example has the whole system at the top with sensible sub-systems at the next level, e.g. Choose film, Choose seats, Take payment, Print ticket (1)
at least one sub-system broken down further, e.g. Take payment → Enter card details, Authorise payment, Issue receipt (1)
questions.model:
A structure diagram is a hierarchical diagram that shows how a system is decomposed into smaller sub-systems, with each level showing more detail.
Cinema ticket system
   Choose film
      Display films
      Select showing
   Choose seats
      Show seat plan
      Select seats
   Take payment
      Enter card details
      Authorise payment
   Print ticket

questions.q:
Write an algorithm in pseudocode, using a WHILE loop, that:
• inputs whole numbers until −1 is entered
• outputs how many numbers were entered (not counting −1) and their total.
ms: initialises Count and Total to 0 (1)
inputs the first number before the loop (1)
WHILE loop with correct condition Num <> −1 … ENDWHILE (1)
increments Count and adds Num to Total inside the loop, then inputs the next number (1)
outputs Count and Total after the loop (1)
questions.model:
Count ← 0
Total ← 0
INPUT Num
WHILE Num <> -1 DO
   Count ← Count + 1
   Total ← Total + Num
   INPUT Num
ENDWHILE
OUTPUT "Numbers entered: ", Count
OUTPUT "Total: ", Total
questions.tip: Input once before the WHILE and again at the end of the loop body, so −1 is never added.

questions.q:
Study this algorithm.
Count ← 0
Total ← 0
INPUT Num
WHILE Num <> 0 DO
   IF Num MOD 2 = 0
      THEN
         Total ← Total + Num
      ELSE
         Count ← Count + 1
   ENDIF
   INPUT Num
ENDWHILE
OUTPUT Total, Count
(a) Complete a trace table (columns Num, Total, Count, OUTPUT) for the inputs 7, 4, 10, 3, 0. [4]
(b) State the purpose of the algorithm. [2]
ms: (a) Total column: 0, 4, 14 (1)
(a) Count column: 0, 1, 2 (1)
(a) OUTPUT: 14, 2 (1)
(b) adds up / totals the even numbers entered (1)
(b) counts the odd numbers entered, until 0 is input (1)
questions.model:
(a)
Num | Total | Count | OUTPUT
    | 0     | 0     |
7   |       | 1     |
4   | 4     |       |
10  | 14    |       |
3   |       | 2     |
0   |       |       | 14, 2
(b) The algorithm adds up all the even numbers entered and counts how many odd numbers are entered, stopping when 0 is input, then outputs the total and the count.
questions.tip: Num MOD 2 = 0 means the number is even.

questions.q:
A teacher enters the marks of 25 students. Each mark must be a whole number from 0 to 100 inclusive; an invalid mark must be re-entered until it is valid.
Write an algorithm in pseudocode that outputs the average mark and the number of marks that are 75 or more.
ms: initialises Total and HighCount to 0 (1)
count-controlled loop for 25 students, e.g. FOR Student ← 1 TO 25 … NEXT (1)
inputs a mark with a prompt (1)
validation loop that re-inputs while Mark < 0 OR Mark > 100 (or REPEAT … UNTIL) (1)
adds each valid mark to Total (1)
IF Mark >= 75 THEN HighCount ← HighCount + 1 (1)
calculates Average ← Total / 25 after the loop (1)
outputs the average and the count with suitable messages (1)
questions.model:
Total ← 0
HighCount ← 0
FOR Student ← 1 TO 25
   OUTPUT "Enter mark"
   INPUT Mark
   WHILE Mark < 0 OR Mark > 100 DO
      OUTPUT "Invalid - enter a mark from 0 to 100"
      INPUT Mark
   ENDWHILE
   Total ← Total + Mark
   IF Mark >= 75
      THEN
         HighCount ← HighCount + 1
   ENDIF
NEXT Student
Average ← Total / 25
OUTPUT "Average mark: ", Average
OUTPUT "Marks of 75 or more: ", HighCount
questions.tip: Calculate the average AFTER the loop, not inside it.
